candidate.answerReason: Expanding both numerator factorials through 9! and canceling the nonzero common factor gives 110-10=100.

methods.label: Expand through the denominator factorial
methods.explanation:
For a positive integer \(n\), \(n!\) is the product \(1\cdot2\cdots n\). Since the denominator is \(9!\), expand only far enough to expose that common factor:
\[
11!=11\cdot10\cdot9!,\qquad 10!=10\cdot9!.
\]
Because \(9!>0\), it can be canceled:
\[
\frac{11!-10!}{9!}
=\frac{(11\cdot10-10)9!}{9!}
=110-10=100.
\]
The value is \(\boxed{100}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: This uses the definition of factorial, a common-factor calculation, and ordinary arithmetic.
